title: Pseudo-superconducting-diode effect in ferroelectric Josephson junctions
authors: Yaozu Tang, Nienke ten Haaf, Artem Bondarenko, Mazhar N. Ali, Yaroslav M. Blanter
abstract: The superconducting diode effect (SDE), characterized by unequal critical supercurrents in opposite current directions, enables supercurrent rectification. We propose a magnetic-field-free pseudo-superconducting-diode effect in ferroelectric Josephson junctions with broken inversion symmetry. Using a coupled dynamical model that combines a polarization-dependent RCSJ description with Landau-Khalatnikov-Tani ferroelectric dynamics, we show that ferroelectric polarization switching induces asymmetric critical and retrapping currents under current sweeps. The resulting nonreciprocity is highly tunable via ferroelectric parameters and the sweep protocol and remains robust at finite temperatures. Our work identifies ferroelectric Josephson junctions as a promising platform for magnetic-field-free nonreciprocal superconducting devices.
summary: The paper theoretically investigates the pseudo-superconducting-diode effect in ferroelectric Josephson junctions by coupling superconducting dynamics with ferroelectric polarization switching. Using a coupled dynamical model solved numerically, the authors show that current sweeping induces nonreciprocal supercurrents due to history-dependent polarization changes. This confirms FE-JJs as tunable platforms for field-free nonreciprocal electronic devices.
main_problem: The authors investigate the pseudo-superconducting-diode effect (SDE) in ferroelectric Josephson junctions, which manifests as nonreciprocal critical and retrapping supercurrents.
main_result: They demonstrate that this nonreciprocity is a history-dependent, non-equilibrium phenomenon arising from current-induced polarization switching, confirming FE-JJs as promising field-free devices.
method: The study employs a coupled dynamical model combining the Resistively and Capacitively Shunted Junction (RCSJ) description with Landau-Khalatnikov-Tani ferroelectric dynamics, solved via numerical simulations including thermal noise.
model_or_system: The physical system is an inversion-asymmetric Ferroelectric Josephson Junction (FE-JJ). The model couples the superconducting phase dynamics ($\phi$) governed by a polarization-dependent RCSJ equation with the ferroelectric polarization ($P$) governed by the LKT equation.
key_observables: Asymmetric critical and retrapping supercurrents ($i_{c\pm}, i_{r\pm}$), diode efficiency ($\eta$), time-averaged voltage, and polarization switching dynamics.
important_parameters: Ferroelectric parameters (e.g., $	heta P_0$), temperature ($T$), and the bias current sweep protocol are crucial for tuning the nonreciprocity.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes validity of linear approximations for critical current dependence on polarization in some contexts, and thermal noise is modeled as Gaussian white noise.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate schematic setups, hysteresis loops showing voltage/polarization under sweeps (comparing P-RCSJ to conventional RCSJ), histograms of currents at finite T, and time evolution during switching events.
paper_structure: The paper builds from defining the coupled dynamical model using Lagrangian formalism, deriving equations of motion for both superconducting and ferroelectric components, simulating current sweeps to observe hysteresis and polarization switching, and finally analyzing the temperature dependence of the resulting nonreciprocity.
why_interesting: This work models a complex interplay between quantum coherence (superconductivity) and classical/emergent order parameters (ferroelectricity), which is highly relevant for understanding open quantum systems where dissipation and environmental coupling drive macroscopic effects.

FIG. 4. Histograms of critical (i± c ) and retrapping (i± r ) currents. The temperature T is set to (a) 0.1 K, (b) 0.2 K, (c) 0.5 K, and (d) 1 K. Each histogram (shown on a log- arithmic scale) is constructed from 1000 full current sweeps. The arrows at the top indicate the zero-temperature values of the critical and retrapping currents for reference. The critical temperature of the superconductor is estimated to be Tc ≃0.5 K using simple BCS approximation.
